purpose: The ONE definition of the mutation method-family taxonomy. Level 2 of class -> family -> realisation -> instance. Every consumer (the per-lane budget in choreo/gen_mutants.py, the paper table tables/method-taxonomy.tex, the coverage ledger, check_class_axis.py) derives from this file instead of restating the family list.
relation_to_class_axis: schema/class-axis.json owns level 1 (the four classes and their lanes). This file owns level 2 (the families inside each class) and does not restate anything class-axis.json already says. Where the two could disagree, class-axis.json wins.
unit_of_requirement_b: (class, method family). NOT spec_id. Requirement (b) -- equal per-lane method count -- is a claim about these 31 cells, and a family is the smallest unit that can be independently not-applicable in a lane.

granularity.class: one compiler UsageType (lib/assess.hpp). 4 of them: M1 ElementAccess, M2 ShapeCompatibility, M3 HardwareConstraint, M4 LoopBound.
granularity.family: one way an obligation of that class can be violated. 31 of them, a-h per class (M4 has 7).
granularity.realisation: one spec_id. A family is realised by 1..n spec_ids; R_f counts the IMPLEMENTED ones.
granularity.instance: one materialised mutant: a (kernel x realisation) program in a lane's corpus.
granularity.budget: N = 4 kernels x 2 realisations = 8 instances per (family x in-scope lane). STRICT: no min(2, R_f) fallback. A family with R_f < 2 is a work item, not a smaller N.

budget.floor_rationale: A class cell is 8 families x 8 = 64 (M4: 7 testable families x 8 = 56; M4-g is restored to the cell as of 2026-09-24). 64 absorbs a 45% noop attrition and still clears 35 admissible. A family with N = 4 would put the cell at 32 and fail the floor, which is why N is not lowered to fit the current R_f.

lane_scope_note: Scope is PER (class x lane x FAMILY), not per (class x lane). in_scope_lanes says which classes a lane runs AT ALL -- that is where a whole-class absence belongs, and it is deliberately NOT restated here. lane_scope says only which individual families INSIDE an in-scope class the lane's surface cannot express; a family listed there is n/a with the prohibition named and is excluded from the lane's denominator. Omitting a family means it is in scope. Decision 2026-09-22: carve-outs are CLEARED -- every in-scope family is targeted at N_PER_FAMILY (8), matching choreo, and no family is excluded from a lane's denominator as derived/absent. A family that cannot in practice be realised is reported as short with its blocker, not pre-excluded. (This restores triton M3 to 8 families and iree M2 to 8: triton 112->128, iree 32->64, total 520->568.) Decision 2026-09-23: M4 is no longer choreo-only -- in_scope_lanes.M4 names all five lanes, so every lane targets M4's 6 testable families. M4-g is withdrawn by `prohibition: "absent"` (nothing can forbid the degenerate pad; M2.12 is `avoided`/repaired) and leaves the cell, so the M4 cell is 6x8=48, not 56, in every lane: choreo 248->240, triton 128->176, mlir-low 64->112, mlir-linalg 64->112, iree 64->112, total 568->752.) Decision 2026-09-23 (same day, revised): M4 is NOT enabled on mlir-linalg/iree. A `linalg.generic`/IREE structured op derives its iteration bound from the operand domain, so the program authors no bound value and M4's detection families (zero/negative/reversed bound, zero step) are inexpressible there -- the prohibition is `derived`. Those lanes hold M4 at `uncompared` and emit no cell; the class is measured only on the program-authored-loop lanes choreo, triton, mlir-low. in_scope_lanes.M4 is therefore the three of them, and mlir-linalg/iree return to their M2-only target: mlir-linalg 112->64, iree 112->64, total 752->656.) Decision 2026-09-24: M4-g (degenerate pad) is RESTORED to the cell. The withdrawal above is reversed: the family carries R_f=2/R_a=2 (choreo M4.7 `negpad` / M4.8 `emptypad`, both `rt-check`), and a new mutation-only kernel is always allowed (channels/README.md), so a lane whose surface does not author a padded extent may still state the degenerate-pad state on its own surface. M4-g therefore leaves the absent set and enters the cell, so the M4 cell is 7x8=56, not 48: choreo 240->248, triton 176->184, mlir-low 112->120, total 656->680. Decision 2026-09-25: cutlass (CUTLASS/CuTe candidate lane) ENTERS the scope model for all four classes -- it is no longer a hand-picked M1/M3/M4 slice with M2 held `uncompared`. Its target is 31 families x 8 = 248, matching choreo, because a hand-written CuTe kernel authors its own index arithmetic (M1), shape/extent contract (M2), TMA/GMMA descriptor and smem capacity (M3), and loop bound/step (M4), so no class is `derived` on this surface. The lane reaches N=8 per family as 4 kernels x 2 realisations, the same decomposition as every other lane; no family is pre-excluded, so an unrealised family is reported short with its blocker rather than carved out. (choreo 248, triton 184, mlir-low 120, cutlass 248, mlir-linalg 64, iree 64; total 680->928. cutlass measured_today 43.)
measured_today_note: Per-lane recorded rows at each lane's last refresh (mlir-low refreshed 2026-09-23 with the v2.1 specs, the M1-a family trimmed to its single-spec budget, M1.20 added to realise M1-g, and the M1-f carrier family M1.19 added over four mutation-only carrier kernels; others as of 2026-09-17), for the delta column. The target is the per-family budget above, not this.
targets_note: Planned total per lane = N x (number of families in scope for that lane). Generated by method_taxonomy.target(); do not hand-edit -- method_taxonomy --check fails if these disagree with the scope model.

outcomes.avoided: the model derives/restores the invariant, or routes around the state. No legal mutant.
outcomes.unexpressible: no legal program states the defect. No mutant.
outcomes.ct-check: legal mutated program; the lane detects it at compile time (warning OR error). Caught.
outcomes.rt-check: legal mutated program; the lane emits a runtime check that can fire. Cost-suppressible.
outcomes.unchecked: legal mutated program; the lane emits nothing. Silent by construction -- where the misses live.

outcomes_note: Canonical across all lanes (mutation-specs-v2.md section 9.6). The retired P1-P4 check-path codes map: P1->rt-check, P2->avoided when the model repairs the state and ct-check when the compiler refuses a well-formed program, P3->unchecked, P4->ct-check. L (launch) is a separate attribution axis (see attribution_only).

admissibility_rule.name: R1-R4
admissibility_rule.rule: A realisation is a TEST only if R1 and R2 and R3 and R4. Otherwise the cell is n/a with the prohibition named and is EXCLUDED from that lane's denominator.
admissibility_rule.R2: independent of the family's other realisation (distinct structural edit)
admissibility_rule.R3: survives repair -- path is not `avoided` and prohibition is not `repaired`
admissibility_rule.R4: attributable -- the spec_id maps to exactly one family (gate `families.partition`)

view_family.why: Extents-equal / layout-unequal: every extent agrees and the affine map does not, so an extent-only shape check cannot decide it. This is the axis BOTH cited corpora name as their top triggering input: 35 of 301 confirmed tile bugs are `Indexing & stride` (TileCodegenBug RC4.1, ISSTA 2026) and 14 of 116 silent torch.compile bugs are `Memory layout conflicts` (arXiv:2604.08720 3.2). It is currently spread across three families in two classes, which is why it is reported as a named tag rather than left implicit.
view_family.report_as: view = M1-b U M1-c U M2-e

M1-a.name: bound / predicate
M1-a.edit: The guard or extent that bounds the address is wrong

M1-b.name: stride / step
M1-b.edit: Step between successive elements is wrong; extents are intact

M1-c.name: origin / offset
M1-c.edit: Base address displaced without shrinking the extent

M1-d.name: index substitution
M1-d.edit: Index expression names the wrong loop variable or mechanism

M1-e.name: tile coordinate
M1-e.edit: Block/tile coordinate is wrong while the in-tile index stays legal

M1-f.name: carrier width
M1-f.edit: Index is legal but the integer carrier cannot name it

M1-g.name: rank / arity
M1-g.edit: Length of the index tuple, or a partition factor, is wrong

M1-h.name: tile overlap
M1-h.edit: Concurrent accesses address the same live slot

M2-a.name: extent value
M2-a.edit: One declared extent is numerically wrong

M2-b.name: extent order
M2-b.edit: Right multiset of extents, wrong permutation

M2-c.name: rank
M2-c.edit: A dimension is added or dropped

M2-d.name: broadcast
M2-d.edit: An extent that must be N is 1, or neither 1 nor equal

M2-e.name: layout (extents intact)
M2-e.edit: Every extent agrees; the affine map does not

M2-f.name: partition
M2-f.edit: Which elements are written is wrong

M2-g.name: padding placement
M2-g.edit: Pad total preserved, placement differs (sum-only check)

M2-h.name: metadata path
M2-h.edit: Contract is skipped because it sits on an unchecked path

M3-a.name: atom divisibility
M3-a.edit: MMA atom M/N/K does not divide the tile

M3-c.name: byte / swizzle box
M3-c.edit: Ceiled byte size, or the box<->swizzle<->alignment relation, is broken

M3-e.name: alignment
M3-e.edit: Base or inner box is not aligned to the required granularity

M3-g.name: pad encoding
M3-g.edit: Pad fields are out of range, or non-zero where forbidden

M3-h.name: on-chip capacity
M3-h.edit: Shared or local tile exceeds the device or per-thread budget

M4-a.name: zero bound
M4-a.edit: A loop extent is 0 -- a legal but empty iteration space

M4-b.name: negative bound
M4-b.edit: A loop bound is negative -- invalid, must be rejected

M4-c.name: runtime-zero bound
M4-c.edit: Bound is symbolic and vanishes only at run time

M4-d.name: empty space
M4-d.edit: Bound is positive but the space is trivially empty (declared noop control)

M4-e.name: reversed bound
M4-e.edit: Upper < lower: overruns instead of iterating emptily

M4-f.name: zero step
M4-f.edit: The iteration variable does not advance

M4-g.name: degenerate pad
M4-g.edit: A padded extent goes negative or empty -- the negative-padding trigger named by the torch.compile study

M1.6.why: Zero-stride / empty range is an iteration-space defect, not an address defect. It was declared under M1 and is counted there today, which double-counts it against M4's control.

M1.7.why: A reversed bound is an iteration-validity defect: the space is not empty, it overruns.

M2.12.why: Rank mismatch through .pad is `avoided` / prohibition `repaired`, so it is NEVER generated and cannot be a realisation. Its negative-padding trigger was re-realised as M4-g. M4-g was briefly withdrawn (`prohibition: "absent"`, 2026-09-23) on the reading that no prohibition forbids a degenerate pad; that withdrawal was REVERSED 2026-09-24 -- M4-g's own realisations M4.7/M4.8 are `rt-check`, and a new mutation-only kernel is always allowed, so the trigger is a live, testable family.

M4.6.why: M4.2 was a single spec_id whose operators already partition by case: 10 set the bound to 0, 4 set it negative. These are two methods with DIFFERENT oracle expectations -- zero is a legal empty iteration space (no error expected), negative is invalid (must be rejected) -- so one spec_id was evidence for two families. Before the split, M4.2 was the sole realisation of M4-b AND one of M4-a's two, so one operator counted in two class cells (defect D1). The split moves the 4 negative cases to M4.6 with no new code.

moves.M4.6: the 4 `negative` cases (M4.6.cv1.negative, M4.6.cv2.neg, M4.6.rl2.neg, M4.6.tp1.neg); operator ids were renamed from M4.2.* so the id and the spec_id agree -- leaving them as M4.2.* would reinstate exactly the ambiguity the split removes

M3-L.why: These carry `path: L` and prohibition `observation`: launch-status and target-limit observations, not value verdicts. They were filed under `cls: M3` in the registry, which puts rows in M3's admissible denominator that M3's claim does not cover -- `docs.no-superseded-claim` in check_class_axis.py already flags the document that says the launch class must not enter M3's admissible N. Kept for attribution, EXCLUDED from M3's 8 families and from M3's class cell.

avoided_never_generated.why: Outcome `avoided` with prohibition `repaired`: the compiler refuses the state or repairs it before the check runs, so the spec can NEVER produce an instance and its verdict is structural, not a gap. These are NOT `unwritten` -- writing them would not create a test. They are the R3 (survives repair) failures. They are also in NO family, which is why they are excluded here.
avoided_never_generated.distinct_from_a_family_member: M3.12 is ALSO `avoided`/repaired but it is M3-h's declared realisation, so it stays in `families` and is reported by the `unrealisable_as_declared` check instead of being filed here. The two buckets must not be merged: this one means 'nothing to do', that one means 'the family needs a different realisation'.
avoided_never_generated.note: M3.12's own registry note records why: 'RECLASSIFIED rt-check -> avoided. memcheck.hpp:106-123 raises Error1 when compile-time SHARED/LOCAL usage exceeds the limit... there is no test to run.' It also names the cause of the 28/40 M3 noops in the committed v1 baseline.

unexpressible_declarations.definition: SIGNED OFF 2026-09-24. Declared in the registry with status `pending` and zero operators, and the model states no legal program that carries the defect: the canonical outcome is `unexpressible` (`u` -- no legal program states the defect, so there is no mutant). These are TERMINAL verdicts, not open work: unlike `dead_declarations`, writing an operator is not the remedy, because the source surface that would state the defect does not exist.
unexpressible_declarations.why: Each carries prohibition `absent` on its registry entry, which is the registry spelling of the same claim. They remain FAMILY-MEMBERS (M1-d, M1-g, M2-h, M3-b, M3-c, M3-e, M4-d) -- the family and its slot are real, the spec_id is what is retired. Do NOT delete them from `families`, and do NOT remove the entry from this ledger: an unexpressible spec that reads as `dead` would send the reader to write an operator that cannot exist. `method_taxonomy.check()` and `gen_mutants.compose()` both subtract this list so the two ledgers cannot disagree.
unexpressible_declarations.distinct_from_dead: `dead_declarations` = the surface is absent from the DSL today, so writing an operator WOULD create a test (e.g. M3.7, whose TMA box geometry is merely unwritten). This ledger = the surface can never carry the defect (the box/swizzle/strided-view/launch-geometry relations the compiler derives rather than reads from source), so no operator is owed.
unexpressible_declarations.basis: User sign-off 2026-09-24 over the pending terminal declarations; see also `outcomes` (`unexpressible`) and `prohibitions` (`absent`).

dead_declarations.definition: Declared in the registry with status `pending` and zero operators, and NOT in p2_never_generated. Writing one of these WOULD create a test.
dead_declarations.why: They make `unwritten` look like work-in-progress when it is an empty set. M3.7 is at once a declaration the source surface has not expressed yet (TMA inner-box geometry is unwritten, not unexpressible) and a FAMILY-MEMBER of M3-e: the family is real and keeps its slot, the spec_id is what is abandoned. Do NOT delete it from `families` -- that would make M3-e look like a family with no declaration at all. The ten specs M1.15/M1.16/M1.18, M2.18, M3.2/M3.3/M3.5/M3.11/M3.13 and M4.4 have MOVED to `unexpressible_declarations` (signed off 2026-09-24): they are terminal, not abandoned work. M3.4, M3.8 and M1.17 have LEFT this list entirely: the rank-5/6 `dma_rank5` re-realisation gave M3-d, M3-f and M1-g operators that the compiler actually assesses. M3.19/M3.21/M3.22 remain here only because they are also `avoided` with no family; `avoided_never_generated` owns their verdict.
dead_declarations.does_not_exist_note: `M2.20` and `M2.22` were carried in the plan prose as dead declarations but are ABSENT from SPEC_REGISTRY entirely -- there is nothing to retire. An earlier dump appeared to skip from M2.19 to M2.21 for this reason, not because of a parse fault.

known_debt.note: Coverage debt that is REAL and TRACKED. `method_taxonomy --check` reports these as DEBT (exit 0) instead of FAIL (exit 1), so the checker is usable as a gate before the debt is paid. The discipline is the same as the `mutants.no-duplicate-injection` ledger: a finding that is NOT listed here is a FAIL (new debt, never seen before); a finding that IS listed but no longer holds is also a FAIL (stale entry). Nothing can be silently added to or removed from this list. Keys are the exact machine keys the checker emits: `<family>:<finding>`.

measured_depth.note: Two orthogonal depths per family, both measured against the registry. R_f is how many realisations exist; R_a is how many of those can serve as a TEST. A family with R_f > 0 and R_a == 0 has operators but no admissible test -- a sharper statement than R_f == 0 and invisible if only R_f is printed.
measured_depth.R_f_definition: spec_ids in the family with status `implemented`
measured_depth.R_a_definition: spec_ids in the family with status `implemented` AND admissible is true AND path is not `avoided`

findings.M3-a: R_f 1, R_a 1, depth 8/8. M3.1 (`MMA contraction extent not divisible by the atom (16)`, rt-check) is the family's only member and is realised on four categories. The two `matmul` realisations (`1_bert`, contraction extent 6 and 10) and the four staging-MMA realisations are numeric corruptions the oracle catches but the current backend does not assess (`never`); only the two `conv2d` `1_attention` realisations (K bumped off the 16-atom) are refused statically (`compile-error`). The staging hosts `lnmma`/`bnmma` carry the `1_bert` GEMM body verbatim into `layer_normalization`/`batch_norm` so the atom obligation lands on two further (spec, category) cells; the remaining M3 categories expose no MMA surface, so the family stops at four categories.
findings.M3-b: R_f 2, R_a 2, depth 8/8. M3.14 (`linear .copy with a dimension >= 2^24`) and M3.15 (`.pad with a dimension >= 2^24`) are both `unchecked` and admissible; M3.2 (`descriptor dimension >= 2^24`, prohibition `absent`) stays unexpressible. The shipped kernels expose M3.14's plain-tile copy anchor only on matmul and both its im2col form and M3.15's pad only on conv2d, capping the family at 3. The staging hosts extend both surfaces without inventing a defect: `lnmma`/`bnmma` carry the plain-tile copy into `layer_normalization`/`batch_norm` (each refused statically, `compile-error`), and the existing pad staging hosts carry the pad anchor into `layer_normalization`/`relu`/`transpose` (each refused at runtime -- the oversize tile trips the smem-limit check before the missing 2^24 check would be reached).
findings.M3-e: R_f 2, R_a 1 after M3.16 was re-homed from M3-c. M3.16 `TMA box inner alignment with a SYMBOLIC leading dim` is `unchecked` and admissible, so it is the family's one test; M3.6/M3.7/M3.11 remain `absent`. M3.16 is a box-alignment defect (F3, `gpu_adapt.hpp:640`), which is why it belongs here rather than in M3-c.
findings.M3-c: R_f 2, R_a 2, depth 8/8. M3.29 and M3.30 (ct-check, the arch-independent swizzle-width and L2-promote byte ladders) are admissible members, so the family's `no admissible declaration` debt is paid and its entry removed. Each is realised once in each of four M3 categories -- `dma_rank5`/r5swiz, `layer_normalization`/lnswiz, `batch_norm`/bnswiz, `max_pool2d`/mpswiz -- reaching the two-cells-per-category ceiling exactly. M3.3/M3.5/M3.13 remain `absent`: their runtime box<->swizzle relation needs group-4, which the sm_86 runner refuses, and a swizzled write read back linearly is a noop there. The ladders are the family's arch-independent half; the runtime relation stays out of scope on this runner.
findings.M3-f: R_f 2, R_a 2, depth 8/8. Two rank-outside-[1,5] surfaces, each realised once in each of four M3 categories. M3.8 (`DMA rank = 6` for `dma.transp`, ct-check) sits on rank-5 `dma.transp` bases -- `dma_rank5`/r5base plus the staging hosts `lnr5trans`/`bnr5trans`/`mpr5trans` -- and M3.31 (`DMA rank = 6` for `dma.pad`, ct-check) on rank-5 `dma.pad` bases -- `dma_rank5`/r5pad plus `lnr5pad`/`bnr5pad`/`mpr5pad`. Each mutation takes the descriptor to rank 6, which the sm_86 backend refuses at compile time (RankLE5, `gpu_adapt.hpp:337` / `:368`). The staging hosts are contrived (rank-5 DMA in MMA-free categories), which is why the runtime rank ladder has no rt-check members.
findings.M4-d: R_f 1, R_a 0 by design -- it is the declared noop control, so its instances must be inadmissible for the admissible floor to mean anything.
findings.M1-g: R_f 2, R_a 2, depth 8/8. M1.17 (`5th-index access on a rank-5 view`, rt-check) carries seven realisations -- `dma_rank5`/r5at plus elementwise rank-5 staging hosts `lnr5at`/`bnr5at`/`mpr5at` in `layer_normalization`/`batch_norm`/`max_pool2d`, two index-off-by-one variants each (off-by-one on the innermost `e` and on the outermost `a`) -- and M1.20 (`view / subspan offset, stride, rank arity`, unchecked) holds `transpose`/tp1. Although M1.17's path class is rt-check, every realisation here is refused statically: semacheck bounds each `.at` dimension, so the mutant is a compile error, not a runtime escape.
findings.M1-f: R_f 1, R_a 1, depth 8/8. M1.19 (`legal index, unnameable carrier width`, unchecked) declares a secondary operand whose extent is lifted into (2^31, 2^32) -- `f32 [K] scale` becomes `f32 [2147483648] scale`. The extent is declared, never materialised, so the base stays usable and each mutant is refused before lowering (an unrepresentable 64-bit extent literal, `unexpected S64_LITERAL`, records as `corrupts`/`compile-error`). The four original carrier kernels (`layer_normalization`/1_bert, /3_attention) plus the staging carriers `smxcarrier`/`relucarrier`/`tpcarrier`/`gelucarrier`/`sigcarrier`/`bncarrier`/`mpcarrier` give one cell in each of eight M1 categories, the family's full one-cell-per-category budget.
findings.M3-h: R_f 2, R_a 2 after the rt-check re-realisations M3.27/M3.28. The declared M3.12 is still `avoided` (compile-time capacity is refused), but a runtime-shaped extent escapes the static check, which is exactly the channel M3-h is about. Before this the family read as unrealisable as declared rather than merely unwritten.

spec_status.note: Defect D2, CORRECTED 2026-09-17. The originally recorded premise was FALSE and is retracted: it claimed that under the two-value enum an `unwritten` spec emits no spec record, so its N/A verdict has nothing to hang on. It does emit one -- `choreo/collect.py::from_spec_registry` walks every entry in the registry snapshot (73 today) and copies `status` through verbatim, so all 23 unwritten specs are represented. Measured cross-tabulation of (status, admissible): implemented/True 49, implemented/False 5, pending/False 23, pending/True 0. Adding a third enum value would therefore unblock nothing: no writer of a new W1 spec needs it. The real defect is a name collision, not a missing value -- `pending` denotes TWO different sets in choreo/mutations.py: the enum value means 'no operator exists' (23 specs), while `pending_specs` -- the GATE 2 list, and the set PATCH-v2.1.md used to gloss as 'admissible, unwritten' -- means 'no operator exists AND admissible' (0 specs). A reader who greps `pending` finds 23 where the gloss promised 0, and `gen_mutants.py --fail-on-pending` reports success without covering 23 of the 23 unwritten specs. Resolution: the gloss in PATCH-v2.1.md is corrected to 'no operator exists; says nothing about admissibility', and mutations.py exports `admissible_unwritten_specs` as an alias of `pending_specs` so a report can state which question it answered. The enum is NOT extended and `pending` is NOT renamed: renaming an existing value would silently change the meaning of every record already written (the `L` -> M3 non-additive hazard) for no gain.
